verdict: Smucker swung from a loss to a $324M profit as about $115M of tariff refunds and derivative gains flattered the quarter, while higher coffee prices lifted sales 5%.

flow.otherDetail: Other income of -$83M is net interest expense of $82M plus $1M of other expense (rounded components; the release total is -$84M before rounding).

takeaways.title: Tariff refunds were the big story
takeaways.text: Gross profit included about $115M of tariff refunds received in the quarter, worth $0.84 of EPS. Adjusted EPS was $3.24, up 71%.

takeaways.title: Coffee carried sales growth
takeaways.text: Coffee sales rose 13% to $808M on higher prices, helping total sales grow 5% to $2.22B even as Hostess sweet baked snacks fell 7%.

takeaways.title: A swing back to profit — with help
takeaways.text: Net income was $324M versus a $44M loss a year ago. The comparison is flattered by a $29M derivative gain this year versus a $253M derivative loss a year ago.

oneTimers: About $115M of tariff refunds received in the quarter, recorded mainly in gross profit, plus $4M of related interest income.
A $29M gain from the change in net cumulative unallocated derivative gains was included in GAAP gross profit (a year ago the same line was a $253M loss).
footerNote: Smucker's fiscal year ends April 30, so this is Q1 of fiscal 2027. Q2 FY27 (quarter ended October 31, 2026) had not been reported as of November 7, 2026, so the latest reported quarter, Q1 FY27, is used. Smucker reports to one decimal place; figures are rounded to whole $M and a few lines sit $1M from their nearest rounding so the statement balances exactly. Segment detail for the International 'Other' line comes from the Form 10-Q segment note.
follow100Note: Lines are rounded to whole $M from Smucker's one-decimal figures, so a few follow-$100 shares may differ by a cent or two from a direct calculation.
